newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa extends losses on arbitrage selling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa extends losses on arbitrage selling.

text.p: London cocoa futures extended losses mainly on arbitrage selling on Wednesday after a slow start to the afternoon. Volumes were slow.
Business was becoming increasingly subdued as market players began to leave for Paris where an annual trade dinner will be held on Friday.
"There is some arbitrage selling, but nothing massive," said one trader.
Light buying by one trading house was cited on outright March positions in the morning session but the initiative was quickly outpaced by sellers.
The most-active March contract lost five stg on the day to 993 stg a tonne but was off its session low of 990 stg. December slipped through 970 support to 965 stg but ended at 966 stg, down seven.
Turnover on the Exchange was a modest 4,748 lots.
Switches were active with May 97/May 98 trading at 63 stg.
Selling from some African origins continued on a small scale, especially as the French franc's weakness kept prices attractive for producers.
This cast against lack of industry buyers who are hoping for new crop arrivals from Ivory Coast to steer prices lower. The new cocoa season starts on October 15.
A strong showing is expected from third quarter European grindings, due out from the end of this week, but traders said these may have already been priced in to the market.
